summary: Thirteen concrete, comment-endorsed finds from the verified 30-story Hacker News front-page crawl.
telegram_footer: 13 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
items.source_story_title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with GPT‑5.6
items.summary: A cost-efficient OpenAI model praised for production reliability and price-performance.
items.why_included: A production user explicitly called its price-performance unmatched and its API reliable.
items.evidence: One production user said OpenAI was their best provider after reliability issues elsewhere, and highlighted Luna's pricing.

evidence_sources.author: __jl__
evidence_sources.excerpt: Luna pricing is crazy now. I don't think there is anything on the market that competes at this price-performance point.

items.name: Orb
items.source_story_title: AI's top startups are barely publishing their research
items.summary: An open-source proactive personal AI backend that connects personal-context signals.
items.why_included: A commenter called the project really cool after its creator described the open-source system.
items.evidence: A commenter described Orb as a promising pairing for a personal-data system they were building.

evidence_sources.author: colingauvin
evidence_sources.excerpt: OK really cool. I've been working on something similar but I started from the opposite direction.

items.name: git-spice
items.source_story_title: Stacked PRs are now live on GitHub
items.summary: An open-source Git tool for creating and managing stacked pull-request branches.
items.why_included: Two commenters independently endorsed it as a focused, low-friction stacked-PR workflow.
items.evidence: One commenter recommended git-spice over Graphite; another said it does exactly what is needed without upsell.

evidence_sources.author: theappsecguy
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'd recommend git-spice, it's very easy to use and powerful, and of course open-source.

evidence_sources.author: perspectivezoom
evidence_sources.excerpt: I will second git-spice. It does exactly what you want and, importantly, no more than that.

items.name: Apple TV 4K
items.source_story_title: Read this before you buy that TV streaming stick
items.summary: A streaming box praised as an ad-free, privacy-convenience compromise.
items.why_included: Several commenters independently recommended it over mainstream smart-TV alternatives.
items.evidence: Commenters praised the ad-free experience and called it the best balance of privacy and convenience.

evidence_sources.author: Mistletoe
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recently got an Apple TV 4K and have been really enjoying the ad free experience. Worth every penny.

evidence_sources.author: MattTheRealOne
evidence_sources.excerpt: Apple TV is currently the best balance of privacy and convenience.

items.name: NVIDIA Shield
items.source_story_title: Read this before you buy that TV streaming stick
items.summary: An older Android TV streaming device still praised for quality.
items.why_included: A commenter gave it a direct, emphatic recommendation despite its age.
items.evidence: One commenter called the NVIDIA Shield pretty damn good even though it is old.

evidence_sources.author: trouve_search
evidence_sources.excerpt: The nvidia shield is pretty damn good as well, even if old at this point.

items.name: The Infinity Machine
items.source_story_title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
items.summary: A reported book about Demis Hassabis, DeepMind, and the AI race.
items.why_included: A reader called it their best book of the current vacation and recommended it for DeepMind context.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended the book as a detailed explanation of DeepMind and other frontier labs.

evidence_sources.author: ddfarmr
evidence_sources.excerpt: I recommend reading „The Infinity Machine: Demis Hassabis, DeepMind, and the Quest for Superintelligence“ from Sebastian Mallaby.

items.name: Litter-Robot
items.source_story_title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
items.summary: An automatic litter box with a long-term owner report of durable use.
items.why_included: The owner reported a decade of use from one model and enthusiastically recommended the product.
items.evidence: One owner said a Litter-Robot 3 was still going strong after ten years and called the machines great.

evidence_sources.author: entropic
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have a litter robot 3 that is still going strong after 10 years,

items.name: Welsh Labs: JEPA and robotics
items.source_story_title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
items.summary: A Welsh Labs video explaining JEPA concepts through robotics.
items.why_included: A commenter directly called the video great while discussing robotics architectures.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended Welsh Labs' video as a great resource on JEPA and robotics.

evidence_sources.author: swframe2
evidence_sources.excerpt: Welsh Labs has a great video on JEPA and robotics.

items.name: Cameron's World
items.summary: A web-art collage built from archived GeoCities pages, text, and images.
items.why_included: It received unusually strong direct praise as a distinctive archival web experience.
items.evidence: A commenter called Cameron's World an absurdly great web mishmash of old GeoCities material.

evidence_sources.author: vunderba
evidence_sources.excerpt: Anyone who hasn't seen it should check out Cameron’s World: an absurdly great web mishmash of text and images from old archived GeoCities pages.

items.name: Hellnet 88x31 Archive
items.summary: A large archive of 88x31 buttons scraped from GeoCities pages.
items.why_included: A commenter specifically suggested it to a fan of web-archive collage art.
items.evidence: A commenter said people who like Cameron's World would probably love this huge button archive.

evidence_sources.author: crumb1e
evidence_sources.excerpt: you'll probably love this then, https://hellnet.work/8831/ a huge archive of 88x31 buttons scraped from the GeoCities archives.

items.name: The Drifter
items.source_story_title: Ron Gilbert started production on Thimbleweed Park 2
items.summary: A modern pulp point-and-click adventure game from Powerhoof.
items.why_included: It received a direct recommendation plus a detailed positive comparison within adventure-game discussion.
items.evidence: Two commenters recommended The Drifter, with one calling it a great modernized adventure-game experience.

evidence_sources.author: wisdomseaker
evidence_sources.excerpt: if anyone hasn't played The drifter yet that is worth checking out

evidence_sources.author: adamesque
evidence_sources.excerpt: The Drifter is a great example of a slightly more modernized take on the classic adventure genre.

items.name: Azul
items.summary: A tile-drafting board game inspired by Portuguese and Moorish decorative art.
items.why_included: It received an unambiguous recommendation for accessible rules and strategic depth.
items.evidence: A commenter called Azul a great board game, easy to start, complex, and heartily recommended.

evidence_sources.author: senko
evidence_sources.excerpt: is a great board game inspired by this style. Easy to start, can get quite complex, heartily recommended!

items.name: Logic for Programmers
items.summary: A practical introduction to formal logic through programming-oriented examples.
items.why_included: A programmer found the sample chapters promising and directly tied their approach to real programming practice.
items.evidence: A commenter said the book looked useful for applying symbolic-logic knowledge back to programming.

evidence_sources.author: rmunn
evidence_sources.excerpt: Seems pretty useful; I'll give the sample chapters a more in-depth read soon.
